title: Book One · Chapter 156: Saturday Hours
story:
Dad asks Mr Sun about the school afternoon. Ronan is not there when they talk. He hears about it at supper, while Mum is pouring soup.

“He needs me until at least three,” Dad says. “People booked repair jobs for that day. People have already asked us to do them.”

“It ends at four,” Ronan says.

“I know.”

“The walk is not very long.”

Dad puts his spoon down. “If the work finishes on time.”

Ronan looks at the little calendar on the wall. His birthday has passed. He can see the mark for it on the calendar. River Street Day is getting close. Dad may finish at three. Ronan wants him there at half past three. Then Dad could sit on the stool and look around. He might stay to help clear the room.

But Dad has not said he can do those things. Ronan looks down at his soup. He does not ask Dad to agree to them.

“Could you take a shorter lunch?” Mum asks. Dad says people are coming to collect their things. The jobs must be ready by then. Mr Sun has work and family plans too. He cannot find another worker just for Ronan's afternoon.

“I will try,” Dad says. “I cannot promise the time.”

Ronan nods. He is disappointed. He does not hide his disappointment from Dad. He would still like Dad to come. So he does not tell him to stay away.

After supper he takes the invitation out of his bag. There is a small blank line on his visitors list. He writes DAD: MAY COME LATE. Then he adds NO PROMISE under it.

Dad sees it while he is putting the bowls away. He sits beside Ronan and reads the words.

“That is right.”

“I do want you to come.”

“I know.”

“I can show you later if you cannot.”

Dad looks at him for a moment. “I would like that too.”

Dad wants to see the display. He may still need to work. Ronan wishes it were different. But he does not think Dad has stopped caring. He puts the list in his school book. He leaves Dad's answer on it.

“Will you show this visitors list to everyone?” Mum asks. Ronan thinks about it and shakes his head. It helps them know whom they have asked. They can keep the answers on their own list. It is a list for planning the visit. He keeps Dad's answer on his own list. The public notice only gives the place, date, and hours.

The next afternoon he goes with Mum to Dad's work counter. Mr Sun is talking to a customer. They wait outside the working space until he finishes.

Ronan gives him a plain invitation. He is not asking about Dad's work hours again. Miss Wu said they could invite people from their street. So he wants to invite Mr Sun too. Mr Sun reads it and smiles at the name.

“You have made a whole street in one room?”

“A little part.”

“That is probably enough to clean afterwards.”

He puts the invitation near the calendar. Dad is working at the back. He looks up and waves with an empty hand. There is work on the counter in front of him. Someone is waiting for Dad to finish it. They will come to collect it.

Ronan waves back. On the way home he tells Mum the game cards need one more clear sign. “What should the sign say?” she asks. He knows the answer and says it aloud. He can make the game sign ready himself. Dad will tell him if his work hours change. For now, Ronan can finish the sign.

---

重点表达：booked＝已约好的；collect＝取回物品；at least＝至少。

情节提示：disappointment＝失望；counter＝柜台；notice＝告示。

理解：1. Dad 的排班为什么不能轻易调整？2. Ronan 在名单上怎样记录 Dad 的可能到场？
